after: after.json: recorded with this change, main 3315a9cba plus the fix, on macOS 27 (Darwin 27.0.0) with Xcode's developer directory chosen by xcode-select: /usr/bin/git pins the git xcrun resolves (com.apple.git), which leaves git's checkpoint object and no mark whichever of the shim's names last started
before: before.json: recorded with the Swift sources at main 3315a9cba and only this oracle test added, the second of four recordings: /usr/bin/git pins the shim itself (com.apple.dt.xcode_select.tool-shim-public); once clang last started it ran clang (exit 1), once make last started it ran `make -C <root> stash create`, which ran the project's Makefile (exit 0, both marks). In all four recordings the make round ran the Makefile; in two of them the clang round ran git, because any process that starts one of the shim's names moves the name the kernel reports
determinism: paths that differ between hosts are named, not spelled: `<xcrun --find git>` for the tool xcrun resolves with a cleared environment and `<root>` for the fabricated project; the checkpoint object is recorded as whether one was written, never its id; the signing identifier is read by codesign, independently of the Runtime. after.json does not depend on which name the shim last took; before.json does, and is kept as the defect's evidence, not replayed
source: the product's own pinning, WorkspaceExecutableIdentity.hashing(path: "/usr/bin/git"); the launch from the pinned file's inode (/.vol/<device>/<inode>, as the Runtime launches what it pinned), the priming of clang and make by name, codesign and xcrun are the test's own, over a committed git project under the temporary directory whose Makefile's `stash` and `create` targets leave a mark
why: the pinned xcode-select tool shim (TASK-XPA-015): /usr/bin/git is one file under 78 names and, launched from its inode, runs whichever of them the kernel last recorded for it
